title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations: catch up with an old friend, get through a family dinner, argue about plans and settle them — joining your ideas into longer sentences and switching between تو, تم and آپ as you go.
intro:
This is where it all comes together. Real conversations don't come one sentence at a time: you catch up with a friend you haven't seen in years, his mother keeps refilling your plate, his sister disagrees with everything, and by dessert you've planned a trip to the mountains.

Two skills make that possible. First, **linking**: joining ideas with **نہ صرف … بلکہ**, **ایک تو … اوپر سے**, **اس سے پہلے کہ**, **چاہے** and the joints you already know. Second, **switching register** on the fly — آپ and تشریف رکھیں for the aunt, تم for the friend, maybe even تو for your oldest mate — without missing a beat.

grammar.title: Linking long sentences
grammar.body:
Fluent speech strings ideas together instead of stopping after each one. You already know many of the joints; here they are together, with some new ones.

**Sequence:**
- **کر** 'having done': چائے پی **کر** 'after having tea'
- **-نے کے بعد** 'after -ing': کھانا کھانے **کے بعد**; **-نے سے پہلے** 'before -ing': نکلنے **سے پہلے**
- **اس سے پہلے کہ** + subjunctive, for a full clause: اس سے پہلے کہ بارش **شروع ہو** 'before it starts raining'. About the past, the -تا form: اس سے پہلے کہ میں کچھ **کہتا**، وہ چلا گیا 'before I could say anything, he'd gone'.
- **جیسے ہی** 'as soon as', **جب … تو** 'when … then'

**Adding:**
- **نہ صرف … بلکہ … بھی** 'not only … but also'
- **ایک تو … اوپر سے …** 'for one thing … and on top of that …' — the colloquial way to pile up complaints

**Conceding:**
- **چاہے** + subjunctive 'whether / even if / no matter': **چاہے** کچھ بھی **ہو** 'whatever happens'; چاہے بارش ہو یا نہ ہو 'rain or no rain'
- **حالانکہ** 'although', **پھر بھی** 'even so'

**Purpose and alternatives:** **تاکہ** + subjunctive 'so that', **ورنہ** 'otherwise', **یا … یا** 'either … or'.

**Style tip:** spoken Urdu prefers chains of short clauses linked with **اور**, **پھر**, **تو** and **کر** over long nested sentences. A few joints used well sound more natural than many used stiffly.

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
In one evening you might talk to your best friend, his grandmother, his little sister and the waiter — and Urdu makes you pick a level for each. Fluent speakers switch instantly, often in the same breath.

**The levels:**
- **تو** + bare stem (آ، بیٹھ، کھا لے) — very close friends of the same age (especially young men), small children. Rude to anyone else.
- **تم** + **-و** (آؤ، بیٹھو) — friends, siblings, younger people. Older relatives use it to you.
- **آپ** + **-یں** (آئیں، بیٹھیں) — elders, strangers, anyone you respect; also many colleagues and couples.
- **آپ** + **-یے / -یے گا** and honorific verbs (**تشریف رکھیں**, **تشریف لائے**, **فرمایا**) — extra polite: guests, elders you want to honour, formal moments.

**Talking *about* people** follows the same rule: respected people take plural verbs even when they're not in the room — ابو **آ گئے ہیں**، دادا ابو **سو رہے ہیں** — while a friend or child is singular: وہ **آ گیا** ہے.

**Signals:** **جی** (جی امی، جی انکل) and **صاحب / جی** after a name raise the level; **یار**, **بھئی**, **اوئے** lower it.

**How switching works:** you switch with the *person*, not mid-sentence to the same person: آنٹی، **آپ** تشریف **رکھیں** … اور **تم**، یار، کچن میں **آؤ**! Mixing levels for one person (آپ … آؤ) is heard in casual Punjabi-flavoured speech, but sounds careless.

**When in doubt, go up a level.** Nobody minds آپ; everybody notices تو.

dialogue.title: Dinner, and a trip to the north
dialogue.setting: Ahmed is back in Lahore after five years in Dubai and has come to dinner at his old friend Bilal's house. Bilal's mother keeps serving; his sister Hina has opinions.

lines.en: Auntie, honestly, this is my third helping! Your cooking… you don't get this in Dubai!

lines.speaker: Bilal

lines.en: Hunza, obviously! Murree's packed for one thing, and on top of that everything's expensive.

lines.speaker: Bilal

lines.roman: tum se kis ne pūchhā? aur Hunza do din kā safar hai, bajaṭ kā bhī socho.
lines.en: Who asked you? And Hunza's two days' drive — think about the budget too.

lines.en: Bilal! Is that any way to talk to your sister? Show a bit of respect.

lines.en: So it's settled? We'll set off first thing Thursday morning.

lines.speaker: Aunty
lines.native: اور اس سے پہلے کہ تم لوگ پہاڑوں پر جاؤ، یہ کھیر ختم کرو!
lines.roman: aur is se pahle ki tum log pahāṛoṃ par jā’o, ye khīr xatm karo!
lines.en: And before you lot head off to the mountains, finish this kheer!

lines.roman: jī ānṭī, ye kām to maiṃ abhī kar detā hūṃ!
lines.en: Yes, Auntie — that job I can do right now!

culture:
**Long conversations** in Pakistani homes follow a rhythm. A guest is welcomed loudly, fed relentlessly (**اور لیں نا!**) and must refuse at least once before accepting more — and saying you're full (**بس، پیٹ بھر گیا**) is a negotiation, not a statement. Elders are greeted first, served first and never contradicted rudely; younger people lower their voices and drop slang around them (**لحاظ**). Siblings bicker freely, and parents step in exactly as Bilal's mother does.

**Register shifts** are constant: young men call each other **تو** and **اوئے**, switch to **آپ** and **جی** the moment an uncle walks in, and to **بھائی صاحب** for the waiter. Girls often call their brothers' friends **بھائی**. In the diaspora, children commonly speak English to each other and Urdu to grandparents — and switch mid-sentence.

**Trips to the north** — Murree, Naran, Swat, Hunza, Skardu — are the classic friends' and family holiday, especially in summer and Eid breaks. And goodbyes take as long as the visit: the 'Pakistani goodbye' starts in the sitting room and finishes, twenty minutes later, at the car door with **رابطے میں رہنا!** and **اللہ حافظ**.

lessons.title: Bumping into an old friend

tip.title: Catching up
tip.body:
- **ارے! پہچانا نہیں؟** · **کتنے سال ہو گئے!** · **برسوں بعد** 'after ages'.
- Get them talking: **اور سناؤ** (friend) / **اور سنائیں** (polite).
- Teasing complaint: **مجھے تم سے ایک شکوہ ہے…**
- Leaving: **رابطے میں رہنا!**

lessons.title: Joining it all up

tip.title: Not only…, on top of that…, before…, whatever…
tip.body:
- **نہ صرف** … **بلکہ** … بھی = not only … but also.
- **ایک تو** … **اوپر سے** … = for one thing … and on top of that.
- **اس سے پہلے کہ** + subjunctive = before: … کہ امی ناراض **ہوں**.
- **چاہے** + subjunctive = whatever / even if: چاہے کچھ بھی **ہو**.

sentences.roman: is se pahle ki maiṃ kuchh kahtā, vo chalā gayā.
sentences.en: Before I could say anything, he'd gone.

sentences.native: ایک تو تم دیر سے آئے، اوپر سے غصہ بھی کر رہے ہو؟
sentences.roman: ek to tum der se ā’e, ūpar se ġussa bhī kar rahe ho?
sentences.en: You turn up late, and on top of that you're the one who's angry?

sentences.native: مختصر یہ کہ ہمیں دیر ہو گئی اور ٹرین چلی گئی۔
sentences.roman: muxtasar ye ki hameṃ der ho ga’ī aur ṭren chalī ga’ī.
sentences.en: Long story short, we were late and the train left without us.

lessons.title: At the dinner table

tip.title: One table, three levels
tip.body:
- Elders: **آپ** + **-یں / -یے**: نانی، آپ شروع **کریں**; انکل، اور **لیجیے** نا.
- Friends, siblings: **تم** + **-و**: دسترخوان لگا **دو**. Very close friends: **تو** + stem: کھا **لے**.
- Talking *about* elders: plural — ابو **آ گئے ہیں**.

new: اور لیں نا، آپ نے تو کچھ کھایا ہی نہیں!

sentences.native: نانی، آپ پہلے شروع کریں۔
sentences.roman: nānī, āp pahle shurūʿ kareṃ.
sentences.en: Nani, you start first.

sentences.native: بیٹا، تھوڑا اور سالن ڈالوں؟
sentences.roman: beṭā, thoṛā aur sālan ḍālūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I give you a bit more curry, dear?

sentences.native: ابو آ گئے ہیں، دسترخوان لگا دو۔
sentences.roman: abbū ā ga’e haiṃ, dastarxān lagā do.
sentences.en: Dad's home — lay out the food.

sentences.native: انکل، آپ اور لیجیے نا۔
sentences.roman: ankal, āp aur lījiye nā.
sentences.en: Uncle, please have some more.

sentences.native: تو بھی کھا لے یار، بعد میں بھوک لگے گی۔
sentences.roman: tū bhī khā le yār, baʿd meṃ bhūk lage gī.
sentences.en: You eat too, mate — you'll get hungry later. (very close friend)

sentences.native: دادا ابو سو رہے ہیں، شور مت کرو۔
sentences.roman: dādā abbū so rahe haiṃ, shor mat karo.
sentences.en: Grandpa's asleep — keep the noise down.

sentences.native: بزرگوں کے سامنے آہستہ بولو۔
sentences.roman: buzurgoṃ ke sāmne āhista bolo.
sentences.en: Speak quietly in front of the elders.

sentences.native: بھائی صاحب، بل لے آئیے گا۔
sentences.roman: bhā’ī sāhab, bil le ā’iye gā.
sentences.en: Could you bring the bill, please? (to a waiter)

sentences.native: آنٹی، بہت مزیدار تھا، لیکن اب بالکل جگہ نہیں!
sentences.roman: ānṭī, bahut mazedār thā, lekin ab bilkul jagah nahīṃ!
sentences.en: Auntie, it was delicious, but I've got no room left at all!

lessons.title: Where shall we go?

tip.title: Arguing without a fight
tip.body:
- Push back: **ضد مت کرو** don't be stubborn · **بہانے مت بناؤ** no excuses.
- Settle it: **چلو، بیچ کا راستہ نکالتے ہیں** · **کیا سب راضی ہیں؟**
- With elders around, keep your **لحاظ** — no **بدتمیزی**.

new: چلو، بیچ کا راستہ نکالتے ہیں۔

sentences.native: ضد مت کرو، سب مری نہیں جانا چاہتے۔
sentences.roman: zid mat karo, sab Marī nahīṃ jānā chāhte.
sentences.en: Don't be stubborn — not everyone wants to go to Murree.

sentences.native: بہانے مت بناؤ، سیدھا بتاؤ کہ نہیں آنا۔
sentences.roman: bahāne mat banā’o, sīdhā batā’o ki nahīṃ ānā.
sentences.en: No excuses — just say you don't want to come.

sentences.native: وہ آخرکار راضی ہو گئی۔
sentences.roman: vo āxirkār rāzī ho ga’ī.
sentences.en: She finally agreed.

sentences.native: کیا سب ہنزہ کے لیے راضی ہیں؟
sentences.roman: kyā sab Hunza ke liye rāzī haiṃ?
sentences.en: Is everyone OK with Hunza?

sentences.native: بیچ کا راستہ یہ ہے کہ ایک دن مری اور دو دن ناران۔
sentences.roman: bīch kā rāsta ye hai ki ek din Marī aur do din Nārān.
sentences.en: The compromise is: one day in Murree and two in Naran.

sentences.native: بھائی سے ایسے بات نہیں کرتے، یہ بدتمیزی ہے۔
sentences.roman: bhā’ī se aise bāt nahīṃ karte, ye badtamīzī hai.
sentences.en: You don't talk to your brother like that — it's rude.

sentences.native: بڑوں کا لحاظ کرو، یار!
sentences.roman: baṛoṃ kā lihāz karo, yār!
sentences.en: Show some respect for the grown-ups, man!

sentences.native: ہر بار تمہاری ضد چلتی ہے!
sentences.roman: har bār tumhārī zid chaltī hai!
sentences.en: You always get your way!

sentences.native: بات یہ ہے کہ بجٹ کم ہے، اس لیے مری بہتر ہے۔
sentences.roman: bāt ye hai ki bajaṭ kam hai, is liye Marī behtar hai.
sentences.en: The thing is, the budget's tight, so Murree is better.

tip.title: Before, after, so that
tip.body:
- **-نے سے پہلے** before -ing: روانہ **ہونے سے پہلے**.
- **-نے کے بعد** after -ing: ہوٹل **پہنچنے کے بعد**.
- **تاکہ** + subjunctive = so that: … **تاکہ** رش سے بچ **سکیں**.
- **چاہے** + subjunctive = even if.

sentences.native: روانہ ہونے سے پہلے گاڑی چیک کروا لو۔
sentences.roman: ravāna hone se pahle gāṛī chek karvā lo.
sentences.en: Get the car checked before we set off.

sentences.native: ہم صبح چھ بجے روانہ ہوں گے تاکہ شام تک پہنچ سکیں۔
sentences.roman: ham subah chhe baje ravāna hoṃ ge tāki shām tak pahuṃch sakeṃ.
sentences.en: We'll set off at six so we can get there by evening.

sentences.native: ہوٹل پہنچنے کے بعد سب آرام کریں گے۔
sentences.roman: hoṭal pahuṃchne ke baʿd sab ārām kareṃ ge.
sentences.en: Once we reach the hotel, everyone will rest.

sentences.native: چاہے موسم خراب ہو، ہم جائیں گے۔
sentences.roman: chāhe mausam xarāb ho, ham jā’eṃ ge.
sentences.en: Even if the weather's bad, we're going.

sentences.native: نکلنے سے پہلے سب کو لوکیشن بھیج دینا۔
sentences.roman: nikalne se pahle sab ko lokeshan bhej denā.
sentences.en: Send everyone the location before you leave.

sentences.native: پہلے بجٹ طے کرو، پھر ہوٹل دیکھتے ہیں۔
sentences.roman: pahle bajaṭ tai karo, phir hoṭal dekhte haiṃ.
sentences.en: Decide the budget first, then we'll look at hotels.

sentences.native: ہر بندے کا بجٹ کتنا ہے؟
sentences.roman: har bande kā bajaṭ kitnā hai?
sentences.en: What's the budget per person?

sentences.native: تمہاری خاطر میں صبح جلدی اٹھ جاؤں گا۔
sentences.roman: tumhārī xātir maiṃ subah jaldī uṭh jā’ūṃ gā.
sentences.en: For your sake I'll get up early. (man)

sentences.native: تو طے یہ ہوا کہ جمعرات کو نکلیں گے۔
sentences.roman: to tai ye huā ki jumeʿrāt ko nikleṃ ge.
sentences.en: So it's agreed we leave on Thursday.

tip.title: Switch with the person
tip.body:
- Pick the level for each person and keep it: آنٹی، آپ تشریف **رکھیں** … اور تم، یار، مدد **کرو**!
- **تو** only with your closest friends: تو کب **آیا**؟
- Extra polite: **تشریف لائے**, **فرمایا**.
- Unsure? Go up a level — **آپ** never offends.

sentences.native: آنٹی، آپ تشریف رکھیں، میں چائے لاتی ہوں۔
sentences.roman: ānṭī, āp tashrīf rakheṃ, maiṃ chā’e lātī hūṃ.
sentences.en: Auntie, please sit down — I'll bring the tea. (woman)

sentences.native: اور تم، یار، کچن میں آ کر میری مدد کرو!
sentences.roman: aur tum, yār, kichan meṃ ā kar merī madad karo!
sentences.en: And you, mate — come and help me in the kitchen!

sentences.native: اوئے، تو کب آیا؟
sentences.roman: o’e, tū kab āyā?
sentences.en: Oi, when did you get here? (very close friend)

sentences.native: انکل، آپ کب تشریف لائے؟
sentences.roman: ankal, āp kab tashrīf lā’e?
sentences.en: Uncle, when did you arrive? (very polite)

sentences.native: ابو سے اس لہجے میں بات مت کرو۔
sentences.roman: abbū se is lahje meṃ bāt mat karo.
sentences.en: Don't talk to Dad in that tone.

sentences.native: نانی جی، آپ کو کچھ چاہیے؟
sentences.roman: nānī jī, āp ko kuchh chāhiye?
sentences.en: Nani, do you need anything?

sentences.native: دوستوں کے ساتھ وہ بالکل بے تکلف ہے، لیکن بزرگوں کے سامنے بہت آہستہ بولتا ہے۔
sentences.roman: dostoṃ ke sāth vo bilkul be takalluf hai, lekin buzurgoṃ ke sāmne bahut āhista boltā hai.
sentences.en: With friends he's totally relaxed, but in front of elders he speaks very softly.

sentences.native: اس کا لہجہ بالکل کراچی والا ہے۔
sentences.roman: us kā lahja bilkul Karāchī vālā hai.
sentences.en: He's got a proper Karachi accent.

sentences.native: چلو، موضوع بدلتے ہیں، کرکٹ کی بات کرو۔
sentences.roman: chalo, mauzūʿ badalte haiṃ, krikeṭ kī bāt karo.
sentences.en: OK, let's change the subject — talk about cricket.
